text:
emma: Hey team — customer (tenant: tenant-624) reports rerank endpoint returning 403 for a model id they claim is valid. Error from their logs:

Customer log:
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "ModelAccessDenied",
  "message": "model reranker_v2 is not accessible for tenant"
}

They said this started after they flipped an alias in their app. Repro steps they gave below. Can someone triage? :eyes:

emma: Repro (their curl):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXX' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-624","model":"reranker_v2","queries":["q1"],"candidates":["a","b"]}'
```

diego: quick check — is that `model` param a tenant-scoped alias or a global id? If alias, routing can map to different underlying models with different perms.

emma: Customer insists `reranker_v2` is their alias (they manage aliases in the console). They also attached a trace id: trace=trc_2026_03_12_77

support-bot: Incident hint: 1) 403 + ModelAccessDenied often means underlying model is flagged for deprecation or is in a different tenant scope. 2) Cache mismatches between alias mapping and permission index are common after alias re-pointing.

olivia: I pulled that tenant's alias mapping from the admin lookup: `tenant-624` alias `reranker_v2` -> global model id `rrk-legacy-2023`. That model has `deprecated:true` and was moved to restricted access earlier this month. So the alias pointed to a model they now lack access to.

emma: ah — so client sees a string that looks the same, but backend resolved it to rrk-legacy-2023 which is restricted. Any quick mitigation? Customer wants a workaround ASAP.

eng-oncall: Options: (1) repoint their alias to an allowed model and invalidate caches, (2) temporarily grant tenant access to rrk-legacy-2023 (not ideal), (3) router change to return 200 with a friendly warning + zeroed scores while we fix (we don't currently do that for permission errors).

diego: To repro locally — we did a call with tenant scope header to emulate: 
```json
POST /v1/rerank
Authorization: Bearer sk-TEST
{
  "tenant_id": "tenant-624",
  "model": "reranker_v2",
  "queries": ["find best"],
  "candidates": ["x","y"]
}

Response:
HTTP/1.1 403
{
  "error":"ModelAccessDenied",
  "model":"rrk-legacy-2023",
  "message":"model rrk-legacy-2023 is restricted for your tenant"
}
```

olivia: I also see an admin event where the alias was updated 2026-03-11 18:02 UTC by svc:alias-manager -> it re-pointed `reranker_v2` from `rrk-optimized-2025` to `rrk-legacy-2023` as part of an automated rollback. Cache TTL for alias lookup is 5m; but permission index re-eval is async and lagged.

emma: Customer says they didn't trigger the alias change from their console — pinging their SRE now.

eng-oncall: Short-term fix I can do: repoint tenant alias back to rrk-optimized-2025 for tenant-624 and purge alias-cache for that tenant. That should restore access immediately. Long-term we should avoid automated rollbacks to restricted models without notifying tenants.

diego: Agreed. Also recommend: 1) add a fast-fail check in router when alias resolves to deprecated model -> return 410 + descriptive message (instead of 403) so customers know it's a deprecation routing issue, 2) surface alias re-point audit in email / console alerts.

emma: I'll coordinate with customer and perform the repoint after they confirm. Customer asked if we can also provide a short postmortem of what caused the automated rollback and how long their production was impacted.

olivia: Logging => alias re-point at 2026-03-11T18:02Z; permission index re-sync completed 2026-03-11T18:09Z (7m lag). Our retention shows ~12 requests failed between 18:03–18:09 for that tenant.

support-bot: Action items pinned: [repoint alias + purge cache], [investigate alias-manager rollback logic], [add clearer routing error codes for deprecations].

emma: Customer confirmed — please do repoint now, eng-oncall. They need it fixed before their morning.

eng-oncall: Done — repointed `tenant-624.reranker_v2` -> `rrk-optimized-2025` and flushed alias cache. Can you validate?

emma: Customer confirmed resubmitted same curl and now gets 200 + expected score array. :tada:

diego: I'll open a ticket to change router behavior and add an alert when alias-manager touches a deprecated target.

olivia: I'll add the audit snippet to the tenant's support ticket with timestamps and number of failed requests.

emma: Thanks all — closing once Olivia uploads the logs to the ticket.
